title: Tom Robbins's banjo band and clown uniforms at age 14
summary: Banjo virtuoso Tom Robbins organizes a banjo band with marimba; Leeman tours theatres at 13-14 in clown uniforms until his father fetches him from Dover, New Hampshire.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, there was a gentleman in my home town -- who Johnny Smith often speaks of, and I don't know whether he's alive or not, his name was Tom Robbins, and he was a kind of, well, erratic sort of person, but he had a basic -- he used to write strange tales, among other things. But he played the x the guitarist
banjo -- he wrote a lot of banjo, he was in all those things in the twenties, he was a banjo virtuoso, and he was also a very strange person.

So we built a base banjo. In those days, they made them to your specifications. And he organized, he gave banjo lessons, among other things, locally, and he took some of his pupils and he organized a banjo band, but he implemented it with the marimba -- he had a big marimba, so as a kid, I was 13 going on 14.
Now what was this man's name again?
Tom Robbins. And for a rundown on him, you could contact Johnnie Smith -- he was a great, he studied with him a bit. Johnnie Smith is from my home town, too.
That's interesting. Great guitarist, just wonderful.
So I went out on the road, we went out for a very short while when I was 14 years old. I was forced to go back to high school, and we went out and did a few what they called the Pantages Theatres?
Right. The Pantages.
We did a few things, and I have pictures of that, of me playing in a clown uniforms -- we all used clown uniforms.
What is that?
Tom Robbins on marimba.
What kind of uniforms did you say you wore?
Clown.
Oh, clown! I see.

Right, and I have pictures of that which are priceless. They had drums, marimba, base banjo, which was a base -- it was strung with bass strings. And all the different -- now I know nothing of plectrum and so forth, but the different sized banjos, and we played popular music with a girl singer.

Well, my father came and got me -- in Dover, New Hampshire, we were playing at the theatre and he said, 'You're going back to school!' -- maybe a little stronger than that, and I went back to high school.
So that's how I started.
Uh huh.

Let's go back to me having a foundation from a good teacher. I tended to read through the Bower method book rather than practice -- I had that in the back of my mind. That's how later on, as I got into music and transgressing with bands, or progressing with bands, I should say, I can explain how my musical ability progressed -- that's the only reason I'm saying that.
And also my Uncle Clifford's drum set and xylophone

was stored in my house -- that hand made xylophone, and I could experiment with it, that's how I, rather than study with my teacher -- I had the foundation, but I would fool around at home to better myself with the basic knowledge.
Now we're in high school now. I'm sorry, I got way ahead of myself.
No problem, Cliff. whatever you want to say.
I just want to do it chronilogically right.
Okay.
